newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan sees no pension-payout inflation surge.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan sees no pension-payout inflation surge.

text.p: Kazakhstan will pay off $477 million in overdue pensions by next year but the move will not spur inflation, the government said. "The republican budget will allot resources worth 36 billion tenge ($477 million), which will be paid to pensioners in six tranches by the end of 1997," a government statement said. And at a press conference National Bank Governor Uraz Dzhandosov said "I believe the pay-off of pensions should not spur inflation." "More than half these arrears is to rural regions of the country, and it is difficult to say how they will react," he said. "But I think there will be no big inflationary pressures."

To finance the pension arrears, the government plans to scrape up an extra 11.6 billion tenge from privatisation and another 8.6 billion tenge by cutting spending on non-urgent needs. Another 7.7 billion tenge is being raised by cutting investment items. It also wants to raise another 8.1 billion tenge on international financial markets.
The1997 budget deficit is expected to widen to 3.66 percent of gross domestic product from an originally targeted 3.16 percent, or to 63.9 billion tenge from 54.9 billion.
The National Bank and the government have targeted 1997 inflation of 17 percent but have said it may be lower.
Dzhandosov said inflation in June was likely to fall to 0.2 percent from 0.4 percent in May. Prices in the first half of the year would grow by 6.1-6.2 percent.

Dzhandosov also said the National Bank was likely to cut base interest rates at the board's meeting on June 30. On June 1 the National Bank cut its refinancing rate to 24 percent annual from 30 percent, Lombard rate to 23 percent annual from 28 percent and the overnight rate to 21 percent from 23 percent. ($1 = 75.42 tenge)
